macro.regime: Cautious, event-dense grind: Hormuz de-escalates, Nvidia/PCE and Jackson Hole all still ahead
macro.narrative: Tuesday 25 Aug's complete US close: S&P 500 +0.32% to 7,677.28, Nasdaq +0.66%, Dow +0.30%, Russell 2000 +0.50%, VIX -2.52% to 15.45 -- a broad, low-vol rally heading into a stacked Wednesday catalyst pile (Nvidia FQ2 after the close, then Core PCE/GDP data). Oil cracked hard (USO -4.58% to $126.15, XLE -1.66% to $62.06) as Iran and Oman floated a proposal for a temporary Hormuz shipping channel, unwinding weeks of built-up geopolitical risk premium even as Beijing publicly criticized the new US sanctions round without being named directly itself. Gold and silver held their debasement-trade grind (GLD +0.32% to $428.07, SLV +0.19% to $62.32) on the same Treasury-buyback dollar-softness mechanism, while Bitcoin pushed above $80,000 for the first time in roughly three months. The day's one hard data print, CB Consumer Confidence, missed meaningfully (89.4 vs 90.3 consensus, down from 90.8, the softest since January) -- a cautionary read on the US consumer heading into today's Core PCE/GDP prints and Friday's Warsh Jackson Hole debut. Net: risk appetite firmed on the Hormuz de-escalation and a cooling VIX, but three consecutive binary catalysts (Nvidia tonight, PCE/GDP later today, Jackson Hole Friday) keep this a cautious, event-dense grind rather than a conviction re-risking.

drivers.factor: Iran-Oman float a temporary Hormuz shipping-channel proposal -- oil craters on the de-escalation
drivers.read: Regional officials confirmed Tuesday that Iran and Oman outlined a plan to jointly establish a temporary shipping channel through the Strait after weeks of fraught talks, materially reducing the geopolitical supply-shock premium that had been built into crude. USO fell 4.58% to $126.15 and XLE fell 1.66% to $62.06 on the news -- a sharper 'sell the de-escalation' move than Monday's 2.5% sanctions-related pullback.

drivers.factor: China criticizes the new Iran-sanctions round without being named directly -- a live but so-far-contained friction point
drivers.read: Beijing said Tuesday the US sanctions threat 'will only further intensify tensions,' a day after Bessent vowed an 'economic D-Day' for buyers of Iranian oil under the phased 'Operation Economic Outcast' framework. China itself has still not been directly designated, keeping this a rhetorical rather than an escalatory risk for now.

drivers.factor: CB Consumer Confidence missed sharply -- 89.4 vs 90.3 consensus, prior revised down to 90.8, softest since January
drivers.read: A meaningful downside miss on the week's one hard US data print, landing hours before today's Core PCE (cons 0.2% m/m, prev 0.1%) and Prelim GDP (cons 1.5% q/q, prev 1.5%) releases at 20:30 SGT -- a cautionary read on the consumer heading into the inflation/growth data that will shape Jackson Hole positioning.

drivers.factor: Nvidia FQ2 earnings land after tonight's close -- the single cleanest live test of AI-capex durability
drivers.read: Street consensus is ~$93-95bn revenue and ~$0.65-0.68 EPS (+67-75% y/y), with analyst price targets clustered $275-325. This is now hours away rather than a day away, and sits back-to-back with the PCE/GDP prints -- the highest-density catalyst stretch of the week for the tech/AI complex.

drivers.factor: Jackson Hole (27-29 Aug) still ahead: Warsh's first keynote as Fed Chair (Fri 28 Aug, 10am ET, theme 'Financial Innovation'), plus Fed speak and the Prelim Benchmark Payrolls Revision (prev -911K) landing Fri 28 Aug 22:00 SGT
drivers.read: Sept-cut odds have swung materially since the July jobs miss (various trackers show anywhere from ~60% hold to ~65% cut priced, underscoring genuine two-sided uncertainty rather than a settled consensus); Warsh's debut is the week's dominant rates catalyst and remains genuinely two-sided into a still price-sensitive tape.
